subject: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>, Nina Kaur <nina@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments

Hi Sam / Nina,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really productive. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed POC/trial plan and the success criteria so we can align on timelines and owners. Below is a concise recap and next steps.

Objective
- Validate Redwood can meet Atlas Payments' latency, throughput, cost, and quality requirements for your transaction-enrichment and customer-service generation workloads.

Proposed success criteria (we discussed these):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference time <= 250ms for live enrichment path (avg payload ~120 tokens).
- Throughput: Sustained 200 req/s during peak batch window (non-burst) with cold-starts considered.
- Cost: <= $0.0009 / token (model + infra) on average for production mix or show clear optimization plan to get there.
- Quality: >= 92% intent-match on your labeled set (sample of 1,200 utterances) and no regression vs your current rule-based outputs in customer-service triage.
- Reliability: <0.5% error rate and graceful fallback to small-model variant under constrained capacity.

Evaluation plan / timeline
- Week 0: Access & test data exchange (we'll send temporary keys + test dataset).
- Week 1: Baseline run — run a synthetic baseline to measure cold and warm latency/throughput.
- Week 2: Joint load test with real-ish traffic and quality eval on labeled set.
- Week 3: Tune batching/quantization and re-run KPIs; hand off a findings doc.

Owners / inputs
- Redwood: Jordan lead (trial setup, kernel/profile work), Marissa (SRE + load testing support).
- Atlas: Sam (POC sponsor), Nina (data + quality labeling contact).

Next steps (action items)
- Sam: share the sample labeled set (S3 link) and a small traffic replay for Week 1 by EOD Wednesday.
- Jordan: send temporary API keys and initial test plan + measurement script by tomorrow.
- Marissa: allocate a load window Wed next week for joint testing.

I'll attach a short MOP (methods of practice) spreadsheet with the measurement cells so we can capture numbers during the run.

If this aligns, I'll convert into a short mutual action plan with dates.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: redwood-poc-mop-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with KPI measurement cells)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@atlaspayments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Kaur <nina@atlaspayments.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments

Jordan — great summary, thanks. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Latency target: 250ms p95 is acceptable but please also include the p99 numbers in your report; our ops team is conservative on tail latency.
- Throughput: the 200 req/s is correct for peak; we may see spikes up to ~300 req/s for short bursts — if you can simulate that it would be helpful.
- Cost: that $0.0009/token target is aspirational; we need an initial estimate vs optimizations. If you can provide an initial cost model after Week 1 that'd be useful.
- Quality: we'll provide the 1,200-sample labeled set by Wednesday. Note: about 60 samples are multi-intent and will need custom scoring — I'll include guidance.

On timing: Wednesday for the sample is fine. I'll get a replay extract of a 2-hour window for your baseline as well.

One ask: can you include expected failure modes and what fallback behavior you recommend? (e.g., deterministic fallback path, smaller-model degrade).

Thanks — Sam

--
Sam Patel
Head of Integrations | Atlas Payments
sam.patel@atlaspayments.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments (planning + ownership)

Marissa / Lauren — forwarding Atlas' confirmations. Please see Sam's notes re: p99, spikes, and multi-intent scoring. Can you confirm:

1) Marissa: you + SRE team to lead Week 1 baseline and Week 2 joint load test? Confirm resource: 4 hours/day of SRE time for test window and a 2-hour dedicated joint load window next Tues.
2) Lauren: can you coordinate the modeling knobs (batching profiles, quantization candidates) and be available for a short 1-hour tune session in Week 3?

Also attaching the current MOP so you can see the measurement cells (I'll push the Sheet to our project folder).

If you can confirm owners + a short checklist, I'll lock the mutual action plan and send to Atlas.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments (planning + ownership)

Jordan — confirmed. Marissa here. 

- SRE: I'll own Week 1 baseline and Week 2 joint load (I'll be lead on the test and will assign 2 SREs for support). We have a 2-hour joint window open on Tue 18 May 14:00-16:00 PT — pls tell Atlas and I'll reserve infra.
- I've attached the SLA draft we discussed (redwood-sla-draft.pdf) and a short checklist for the baseline run.

Checklist highlights:
- Validate API keys + rate limits
- Run cold-start baseline (3 cold starts)
- Run warm-start sustained 10-minute window at nominal load
- Run spike test up to 320 req/s for 2 minutes to observe degradation/fallback
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates, plus CPU/GPU utilization

Lauren — can you confirm availability for Week 3 tuning session?

—Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: POC success criteria & trial KPIs — Atlas Payments (mutual action plan + next steps)

Sam / Nina — thanks again. Per internal sync we've locked owners and a joint test window. Quick summary and confirmed next steps: 

Confirmed items:
- Joint test window: Tue 18 May 2027 14:00-16:00 PT (Marissa + SRE team will run; please confirm this works on your side).
- Deliverables from Atlas by Wed 12 May EOD: labeled set (1,200 samples) and 2-hour traffic replay extract.
- Redwood deliverables by Mon 17 May EOD: temporary API keys, initial measurement script, and a preliminary cost model (ballpark).
- Success criteria: p95 <= 250ms, include p99 in report; sustained 200 req/s with ability to observe spikes to 320 req/s; cost target <= $0.0009/token with optimization plan; quality >=92% on labeled set (we'll use your multi-intent scoring guidance).

Action items (owners):
- Sam: confirm joint window + share data links (S3) for labeled set + replay.
- Marissa: reserve infra + publish the baseline checklist (done).
- Lauren: prepare tuning run and join Week 3 session (we're targeting Wed 26 May 10:00-11:00 PT for tuning).
- Jordan: send mutual action plan doc and a short measurement worksheet (sheet link included).

Fallback modes: we will run with a deterministic small-model fallback (lower-cost embed-only path) and a N+1 replica policy to reduce error impact. We'll document these in the findings doc.

If that looks right, please reply with a quick "ack" and I'll move the MAP into HubSpot and schedule the calendar invites.

Thanks — Jordan
